content.title: Tiger Woods’ mugshot released after his arrest
content.text: Golf player charged with driving under the influence after a crash near his home in Florida. Police said he appeared to be on ‘some type of medication or drug’ Tiger Woods stands by his overturned vehicle in Florida, left, and Woods’s mugshotMartin County Sheriff’s Office/AP Saturday March 28 2026, 2.30am GMT, The Times Police have released Tiger Woods’ mugshot after he was charged with driving under the influence following a crash near his home in Jupiter, Florida. The golf superstar, 50, attempted to overtake a truck carrying a pressure cleaner at a “high rate of speed” and rolled his car on to its side at about 2pm on Friday, Sheriff John Budensiek of Martin County said. Woods took a breathalyser test and showed no signs of having consumed alcohol. However, he did “exemplify signs of impairment” and refused a urine test. Budensiek said he appeared to be on “some type of medication or drug”, but gave no further details. Tiger Woods stands by his overturned vehicle in FloridaJASON OTERI/AP Skid marks near the overturned vehicleMARTIN COUNTY SHERIFF’S OFFICE/AP “When it came [to the] time for us to ask for a urinalysis test, he refused, and so he’s been charged with DUI [driving under the influence], with property damage and refusal to submit to a lawful test in the crash,” Budensiek said. Woods was not injured but was “lethargic” on the scene and was alone in the car before he crawled out of the passenger door. He was arrested and then booked at a local jail, police said. Under Florida law, he had to remain in jail for at least eight hours before being released on bond. Pictures showed Woods leaving the Martin County jail around midnight local time. Tiger Woods is driven from the Martin County JailJoe Raedle/Getty Images Photographs from the scene of the crash showed the vehicle lying on the driver’s side. • Sign up for The Times’s weekly US newsletter When describing how the crash occurred on a small, two-lane road, Budensiek said: “Had there been someone moving in the opposite direction, we would not be having a conversation saying there were no injuries.” Tiger Woods is arrested on charge of driving under the influence after Florida crash The sheriff added: “This could have been a lot worse.” Asked how quickly Woods had been driving in the run-up to the accident, Budensiek told reporters he was unable to estimate the speed, but added: “I can tell you this, it’s a 30-mile-an-hour speed limit. “When I show you the photos, they kind of speak for themselves … you can see that he slid for a decent space before he came to a stop.” MARTIN COUNTY SHERIFF’S OFFICE/AP Before the crash, it had seemed likely that Woods might make a return to competitive golf at the Masters from April 9. However, this is the latest incident in a long list of his mishaps behind the wheel. In November 2009, he suffered facial injuries after colliding with a fire hydrant, a tree and hedges when driving from his Florida mansion late at night. He was penalised for careless driving and two weeks later took an indefinite break from professional golf after admitting to a string of extramarital affairs. Although Woods returned with successes on the PGA Tour, he was arrested in 2017, also near his home on Jupiter Island, after he was found asleep in his car blocking a stationary line of traffic with his engine running. Dashcam footage showed him incapable of walking straight on a white line when asked to do so by a police officer. Although Woods said he took a mixture of prescription drugs without realising how they could affect each other, he pleaded guilty to reckless driving five months later and issued a public apology. A police mugshot after Woods’s 2017 accidentPalm Beach County Sheriff’s Offi/AFP/Getty Images Woods returned after five major operations on his left knee, going on to win the 2019 Masters almost 11 years after his previous major triumph. However, he suffered serious leg injuries when his car flipped off the road in California in February 2021. Woods was driving close to double the 45mph speed limit and doctors considered amputating his right leg after he was extricated from the wreck by firefighters and paramedics. He had a rod inserted in his tibia to repair compound fractures as well as screws and pins to fix his shattered ankle. There was no evidence that he had been under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Despite the severity of the crash and his now notable limp, Woods made his 23rd consecutive cut at the Masters in 2023, but he has played only seven majors since, missing four cuts, withdrawing twice and finishing 60th in the other. Having spent 683 weeks as the top player in the world, he is now ranked number 3,483. The aftermath of the 2009 accident It was therefore telling when news emerged on Friday that Woods had registered for this year’s US Senior Open, a notable event given that he missed all last season after surgery to repair a ruptured Achilles tendon. He also underwent a seventh back operation last October. “I’ve been trying [to play in this year’s Masters],” Woods said. “Just this body, it doesn’t recover like it did when it was 24, 25. It doesn’t mean I’m not trying. I’ve been trying a while. “I’ve had a couple of bad injuries last year that I’ve had to fight and it has taken some time. I want to play. I love the tournament. I’ll be practising and playing at home this week and keep trying to make progress.” After this latest arrest his presence at this year’s Masters — possibly even in the clubhouse as a former champion — seems out of the question.
